title: Titanium Sintered Filter Element
alloyReason: Grade 2 CP-Ti (UNS R50400) is selected for Titanium Sintered Filter Element where formability and corrosion resistance are prioritized over absolute strength. With 40% elongation and excellent weldability, Grade 2 CP-Ti forms a stable TiO₂ passive film that provides immunity to pitting in chloride environments up to 260°C. Its 345 MPa yield strength with 30% elongation makes it ideal for Sintered titanium porous filter element requiring cold forming or bending without cracking. This rationale is driven by sintered titanium porous filter element and specific design requirements.
process: CNC machining from plate for filtration geometry
TIG welding all-position for net-shape tolerance
Passivation DI rinse for net-shape tolerance
surfaceTreatment: Pickling HF-HNO3 bath + passivation to restore passive film integrity on welded/seamed process surfaces — tailored for sintered titanium porous application
commonFailures: Crevice corrosion under gasket in wet service - mitigated by raised-face flange design per ASME B16.5 — critical for sintered titanium porous performance

faq.q: What pH range can Titanium Sintered Filter Element withstand in effluent streams?
faq.a: Grade 2 CP-Ti maintains corrosion rates below 0.05 mm/year across pH 2-12 at 40°C in chloride-containing effluents. For sintered titanium porous handling acidic or alkaline waste streams, titanium eliminates the need for polymer linings or acid-resistant brick, reducing maintenance costs by approximately 60% over the 10-year design life.
